summary.text: Case 1, aged 52 y in Table 1, had a melanoma of the instep (Breslow thickness 8 mm and Clark level IV), with diabetes listed as a comorbidity. The resection margin was 2 cm and the sentinel node biopsy was positive. A secondary inguinal lymph node dissection was performed, and the table records recurrence or metastasis as Yes.

Melanoma resection and primary reconstruction with a reverse sural artery flap were performed from 2006 to 2009, with primary closure of the donor site. All flaps were harvested including the medial sural nerve, lesser saphenous vein and deep fascia, all pedicles were at least 3 cm wide, and mild venous congestion was noted during the first postoperative week in all cases.

A mild cellulitis of the thigh was perceived and oral antibiotics were required. After a minimal 5-year follow-up (Table 1: 74 mo) limb function had completely recovered, cosmetic results were acceptable, and some numbness in the sural nerve dermatome area was not considered relevant.
